group_assessment.weighting: Twenty male Wistar rats (four groups of five) weaned at postnatal day 21, 15% caloric restriction for about 55-64 days, amygdala kindling, western blots and qPCR in hippocampus and temporal neocortex. The kindled and non-kindled animals were pooled into n = 10 per diet for the molecular data after showing they did not differ. The observation (higher after-discharge threshold, lower pPKB and pS6 under mild restriction; no change in kindling rate, glucose, beta-hydroxybutyrate or insulin) is firm as reported for this design; the inference that mTOR inhibition causes the anticonvulsant effect is correlational (tissue taken after kindling, one time point). Not a WWOX system and not a neonatal or feeding-protocol model.

entries.proposition: The restriction was mild (15%) and given without vitamin or mineral supplementation to young rats.
entries.snippet: CR was accomplished by food restriction without vitamin or mineral supplementation; therefore the rats were subjected to mild CR (15%) to avoid any concerns relating to under-nutrition, especially given their young age.

entries.proposition: Kindled and non-kindled animals were pooled for the molecular data (AL n = 10, CR n = 10); the four starting groups held five animals each (Methods group-assignment sentence, not quoted).
entries.snippet: Thus, control and kindled control data were pooled together (hereafter AL, n = 10) and the results for experimental and kindled experimental rats were combined (henceforth CR, n = 10) for all subsequent analysis.

contradicts_locator.what_changed: five-per-cell attributed to the Methods sentence, not the quote

entries.proposition: Restriction raised the after-discharge threshold and shortened after-discharge duration on three days only.
entries.snippet: CR significantly increased [t(1, 8) = −3.35, p = 0.01] the AD threshold (Figure 3A) and reduced the AD duration in days 14 [t(1, 8) = 2.73, p < 0.05], 15 [t(1, 8) = 4.63, p < 0.01] and 16 [t(1, 8) = 2.92, p < 0.05] of the kindling procedure (Figure 3B).
entries.anchor: Results, Electrical kindling of the amygdala

entries.proposition: Figure 3A shows the CR threshold about 160% of the ad libitum value with a wide error bar and two asterisks; Figure 3B shows the duration curves close for days 1-12, CR points below ad libitum on days 13-16 (asterisks on days 14-16) and ad libitum points again higher on days 21-24 without asterisks.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 3: panel A, after-discharge threshold (%), ad libitum 100 and CR near 160 with a wide error bar and two asterisks; panel B, after-discharge duration (s) against day of kindling, curves close for days 1-12, CR below ad libitum around days 13-16 with asterisks on days 14-16, ad libitum points higher again on days 21-24 without asterisks.

experimental_context.system: young male Wistar rat, 15% caloric restriction, amygdala kindling

contradicts_locator.what_changed: panel B description corrected: not overlapping after day 16

entries.proposition: Apart from the after-discharge threshold and the after-discharge duration on days 14-16, restriction did not alter the kindling rate or any other kindling parameter.
entries.snippet: However, CR did not significantly alter the AD duration in any other day nor did it affect any other kindling parameter

entries.proposition: The authors read the profile as anti-convulsant, not anti-epileptogenic.
entries.snippet: This suggests an anti-convulsive profile rather than an anti-epileptogenic action; which is totally independent from changes in glucose, insulin or β-HB.

entries.proposition: Fasting-state glucose, beta-hydroxybutyrate and insulin did not differ between restricted and ad libitum rats.
entries.snippet: On the other hand, fasting blood glucose and β-HB as well as plasma insulin (Figure 2) were similar between the groups

entries.proposition: Figure 2: blood beta-hydroxybutyrate near 0.9 then 0.55 mmol/l, glucose near 85 then 123 mg/dl, insulin near 1.4 ng/ml, with no difference between diets.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 2: panel A beta-hydroxybutyrate about 0.9 initial and 0.55 mmol/l final in both diets; panel B glucose about 85 initial and 123 mg/dl final in both diets; panel C plasma insulin about 1.4 ng/ml, bars for the two diets level within error.

experimental_context.system: young male Wistar rat after a 4 h fast

entries.proposition: Restriction significantly reduced pPKB and pS6 in cortex and hippocampus; the hippocampal pAMPK rise (p < 0.05) and the nonsignificant cortical trend (p = 0.16) are in the preceding sentence, not quoted.
entries.snippet: CR significantly reduced PKB/Akt and S6 phosphorylation in the Cx [PKB: t(1, 18) = 3.03, p < 0.01 and S6: t(1, 18) = 2.13, p < 0.05] and Hp [PKB: t(1, 18) = 3.13, p < 0.01 and S6: t(1, 18) = 2.39, p < 0.05], suggesting that CR inhibited the mTOR cascade.

contradicts_locator.what_changed: proposition restricted to PKB and S6 as quoted; AMPK attributed to the adjacent sentence

entries.proposition: Figure 5 shows pPKB/PKB and pS6/S6 lower under restriction in both regions, with pAMPK/AMPK higher in hippocampus only.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 5: panel A pAMPK/AMPK about 1.3 versus 1.5 with an asterisk only in hippocampus; panel B pPKB/PKB lower in both regions (two asterisks); panel C pS6/S6 lower in both regions (one asterisk), with a wide error bar on the neocortical ad libitum bar.

entries.proposition: The mTOR readout was taken after the kindling series, so the state of the pathway at the time of the threshold measurements is unknown.
entries.snippet: Thus, the status of the mTOR pathway in the amygdala when the after-discharge threshold (postnatal day 55) and duration (postnatal days 55–75) were determined is unknown.

entries.proposition: Even mild restriction reduced weight gain in weanling rats, which the authors say may limit use in children.
entries.snippet: Unfortunately, even mild CR significantly reduced weight gain in weanling rats which may limit its use in children and adolescents due to concerns regarding their growth.
entries.anchor: Discussion, mTOR signaling cascade, last paragraph

entries.proposition: All rats progressed to generalised seizures at the same kindling rate; the authors say in the next sentence that this was probably due to the low degree of restriction (a hedge, not a finding).
entries.snippet: In addition, despite the presumed inhibition of the mTOR pathway all the rats progressed to generalized convulsive seizures with the same kindling rate.
entries.anchor: Discussion, mTOR signaling cascade, last paragraph

entries.proposition: The authors conclude the effects were likely independent of glucose, beta-hydroxybutyrate, insulin and gene expression; the species and duration caveats on glucose and ketone effects are in the Discussion elsewhere, not in the quote.
entries.snippet: The effects of CR were likely independent from any changes in glucose, β-HB, insulin or gene expression (AMPKα1, AMPKα2, mTOR, S6K, TSC1, or TSC2) since none were modified by CR.
